title: Generation of nephron progenitor cells and kidney organoids from human pluripotent stem cells
markdown:
## Protocol: Generation of kidney organoids from human pluripotent stem cells

### Overview

This protocol details the generation of kidney organoids from human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs). It covers reagent preparation, hPSC maintenance and passaging, preparation for differentiation, induction of posterior intermediate mesoderm, conversion to neural plate border/nephric progenitor cells (NPCs), and subsequent differentiation into either 2D or 3D kidney organoids. Key critical steps include monitoring cell confluency, morphology changes during differentiation, and optimizing plating densities and growth factor concentrations based on specific cell lines.

### Materials/Reagents

Advanced RPMI 1640, L-GlutaMAX, DMEM/F12, LDEV-Free hESC-qualified Geltrex, PBS, Triton X-100, PBST, Bovine Serum Albumin (BSA), Donkey Serum, Paraformaldehyde (PFA), FGF2, CHIR99021 (CHIR), Noggin, Dorsomorphin, Activin A, FGF9, Y27632, Cisplatin, ReproFF2 medium, Dissociation Solution for human ES/iPS cells (CTK solution), Accutase.

### Equipment

Refrigerator (4°C), Freezer (-20°C), 37°C CO2 Incubator, Clean Bench, Cellometer Counting Chamber, 15 ml tubes, 6-well plates, 24-well plates, 96-well round bottom ultra-low-attachment plates, 1 ml pipettes, 200 μl pipettes, cell scraper.

### Safety & Sterility

Keep Geltrex on ice to avoid solidification. Use sterile techniques throughout. Handle PFA and other chemical reagents with appropriate safety precautions. Ensure all solutions are prepared in sterile conditions where applicable.

## Reagent Preparation

### Preparation

1. Make 45 ml aliquots of the medium and store at −20 °C for up to 6 months. Thaw an aliquot in a refrigerator overnight, add FGF2 to a final concentration of 10 ng/ml, keep the medium at 4°C, and use within one week. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S01 -->
2. Mix solution A and solution B, make 45 ml aliquots, and store at −20 °C for up to 6 months. Thaw an aliquot in a refrigerator overnight, add FGF2 to a final concentration of 10 ng/ml, keep the medium at 4°C, and use within one week. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S02 -->
3. Add 5 ml L-GlutaMAX to 500 ml advanced RPMI 1640. Keep the medium at 4°C and use within one month. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S03 -->
4. Add LDEV-Free hESC-qualified Geltrex to cold DMEM/F12 at a 1:100 ratio. Add 1 ml total volume per well of a 6-well plate or 300 μl per well of a 24-well plate. Incubate coated plates at 37 °C for at least one hour. Store coated plates at 4°C and use within one week. Before seeding cells, place plates on a clean bench for at least 30 minutes at room temperature (20–25 °C). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S04 -->
> **Operational constraint:** **CAUTION**: Keep Geltrex on ice to prevent it from solidifying. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S05 -->
5. Add 1.5 ml Triton X-100 to 500 ml PBS and shake well. Keep at room temperature and use within 12 months. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S06 -->
6. Add 400 mg bovine serum albumin to 40 ml PBST and shake well. Keep at 4°C and use within one month. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S07 -->
7. Add 1 ml donkey serum to PBST and shake well. Keep at 4°C and use within two weeks. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S08 -->
8. Add 10 ml 16% PFA to 30 ml PBS. Keep at 4°C and use within two weeks. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S09 -->
9. Reconstitute 100 μg FGF2 in 10 ml PBS containing 0.1% (w/v) BSA. Make small aliquots and store at −20 °C for up to 6 months. After thawing, store the aliquot at 4°C and use within one week. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S10 -->
10. **CHIR (10 mM)**: Reconstitute 10 mg CHIR in 2.149 ml DMSO. Make small aliquots (60 μl) and store at −20 °C for up to 6 months. After thawing, store the aliquot at 4°C and use within one week. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S11 -->
11. **Noggin (100 μg/ml)**: Reconstitute 20 μg noggin in 200 μl PBS containing 0.1% (w/v) BSA. Make small aliquots (10 μl) and store at −20 °C for up to 6 months. After thawing, store the aliquot at 4°C and use within two weeks. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S12 -->
12. **Dorsomorphin (10 mM)**: Reconstitute 10 mg dorsomorphin in 2020 μl DMSO. Make small aliquots (50 μl) and store at −20 °C for up to 12 months. After thawing, store the aliquot at 4°C and use within one week. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S13 -->
13. **Activin A (50 μg/ml)**: Reconstitute 50 μg activin A in 1 ml PBS. Make small aliquots (20 μl) and store at −20 °C for up to 12 months. After thawing, store the aliquot at 4°C and use within two weeks. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S14 -->
14. **FGF9 (100 μg/ml)**: Reconstitute 25 μg FGF9 in 250 μl PBS containing 0.1% BSA. Make small aliquots (10 μl) and store at −20 °C for up to 6 months. After thawing, store the aliquot at 4°C and use within two weeks. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S15 -->
15. **Y27632 (10 mM)**: Reconstitute 10 mg Y27632 in 3.0792 ml PBS. Make small aliquots (80 μl) and store at −20 °C for up to 6 months. After thawing, store the aliquot at 4°C and use within one week. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S16 -->
16. **Cisplatin (5 mM)**: Reconstitute 15 mg cisplatin in 10 ml sterile water. Make small aliquots and store at −20 °C for up to 6 months. After thawing, store the aliquot at 4°C and use within two weeks. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S17 -->

## Cell Preparation and Plating

### 15 min in total

1. After a total incubation time of 15 minutes, gently detach and dissociate the cells using a 1 ml pipette until no cell aggregates are visible. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S89 -->
2. Prepare 15 ml tubes by adding 500 μl ReproFF2 to each tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S90 -->
3. Collect the dissociated cells into the 15 ml tubes containing 500 μl ReproFF2. Take a 20 μl sample from the tubes to a Cellometer Counting Chamber for cell counting. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S91 -->
4. Centrifuge the tubes at 300 g at room temperature for 4 minutes. While centrifuging, count the cells using a Cellometer. Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet at a density of 10,000 cells/μl in ReproFF2. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S92 -->

### Post-centrifugation / Pre-plating

1. Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the cells at 10,000 cells/μl in ReproFF2. Prepare sufficient ReproFF2 supplemented with 10 μM ROCK inhibitor Y27632 (1:1000 dilution) for differentiation experiments. Transfer the cell suspension into this medium to achieve a final density of 44,000–86,000 cells/ml (equivalent to 12,000–24,000 cells/cm²). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T1-S01 -->
2. Plate the cell suspension at a volume of 500 μl per well in 24-well plates. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T1-S02 -->
> **Operational constraint:** **Constraint**: Plating density is critical for high differentiation efficiency. Test different densities for different cell lines. For H9 cells, ~20,000 cells/cm² is optimal; for HDF-α iPS cells, ~14,000 cells/cm² is optimal. Well size also impacts efficiency; adjust densities if changing well sizes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T1-S03 -->

### 72 hours post-plating

1. Culture the cells at 37 °C in a 5% CO₂ incubator for 72 hours without changing the medium. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T2-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** If you want to start the differentiation earlier, you need to plate more cells at step 12 to have nearly 50% confluent cells when you start the differentiation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T2-S02 -->

## Differentiation Initiation

### 2~3 days post-initiation

1. Culture the cells at 37 °C in a 5% CO₂ incubator for 2–3 days without feeding the cells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** **Constraint**: If SIX2+ cell induction is insufficient, test treating with activin A for 2 days instead of 3 days. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S02 -->

### 96 h

1. **Evaluation**: Typically, 96 hours of differentiation is the optimal timing, but this can be adjusted based on cell morphology. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S94 -->
2. Aspirate the existing medium and add 750 μl of differentiation medium containing 10 ng/ml activin A. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S95 -->
> **Operational constraint:** **Constraint**: This stage is critical for efficient NPC differentiation. Carefully check morphology. If cells form a homogenous flat monolayer (too loose), feed with differentiation medium containing the same CHIR concentration (with or without BMP4 inhibitor) and wait 0.5–1 day. If cells form dome-like round clusters similar to undifferentiated mouse embryonic stem cells (too dense), it may be too late; restart differentiation with lower CHIR concentration. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S96 -->

## Differentiation into 2D Kidney Organoids

### 12~ d

1. Aspirate the medium and add 500 μl–1 ml of differentiation medium containing 10 ng/ml FGF9 and 3 μM CHIR. **Critical Step**: Check morphology. If many cells form round polarized structures with lumens resembling renal vesicles, shorten the treatment time of this step from 2 days to 1 day. If the medium turns yellow quickly, increase the medium volume to 1 ml in future experiments. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S01 -->
2. Culture the cells at 37 °C in a 5% CO₂ incubator for 2 days. **Critical Step**: If the medium turns yellow after 1 day, feed the cells with differentiation medium containing the same concentrations of CHIR and FGF9 and the same volume as in the previous step. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S02 -->
3. Aspirate the medium and add 750 μl–1 ml of differentiation medium containing 10 ng/ml FGF9. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S03 -->
4. Culture the cells at 37 °C in a 5% CO₂ incubator for 2–3 days. Proceed to the next step if round polarized structures with lumens resembling renal vesicles are observed. If not observed within 3 days, confirm LHX1 expression via immunostaining; proceed if most cells are LHX1 positive. **Critical Step**: If the medium turns yellow after 1–2 days, feed with differentiation medium containing the same FGF9 concentration and volume as in the previous step. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S04 -->
5. Aspirate the medium and add 500 μl of basic differentiation medium without growth factors. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S05 -->
6. Feed cells every 2–3 days with 500–750 μl of basic differentiation medium. Kidney organoids remain stable for at least 3 months. Nephron structures can be visualized under a microscope. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S06 -->

## Differentiation into 3D Kidney Organoids

### 12~ d

1. Aspirate the medium and add 500 μl PBS to wash out residual differentiation medium. Aspirate PBS and add 300 μl Accutase per well of the 24-well plate. Incubate at 37 °C in a 5% CO₂ incubator for 10–15 minutes. Meanwhile, prepare 15 ml tubes containing 300 μl of basic differentiation medium supplemented with 3 μM CHIR and 10 ng/ml FGF9. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T0-S01 -->
2. Dissociate the cells using a 1 ml pipette and transfer them to the prepared 15 ml tubes. Take a 20 μl sample from the tubes for cell counting with a Cellometer. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T0-S02 -->
3. Centrifuge the tubes at 300 g at room temperature for 4 minutes. Count the cells. Aspirate the medium and resuspend the cells in the supplemented basic differentiation medium at a density of 500,000 cells/ml. Plate 100,000 cells per well in 200 μl of differentiation medium onto 96-well, round-bottom, ultra-low-attachment plates. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T0-S03 -->
4. Centrifuge the plates at 300 g for 15 seconds. Culture the cells at 37 °C in a 5% CO₂ incubator for 2 days. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T0-S04 -->
5. Gently aspirate the medium using a 200 μl pipette and add 200 μl of basic differentiation medium supplemented with 10 ng/ml FGF9. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T0-S05 -->
6. Culture the cells at 37 °C in a 5% CO₂ incubator for 2–3 days until renal vesicle-like round structures become visible under a microscope. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T0-S06 -->
7. Aspirate the medium using a 200 μl pipette and add basic differentiation medium without any additional growth factors. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T0-S07 -->
8. Culture the cells at 37 °C in a 5% CO₂ incubator for at least 1 week. Every 2–4 days, aspirate 85 μl of medium and add 100 μl of basic differentiation medium. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T0-S08 -->

## Differentiation into NPCs

### 1~2 d

1. Aspirate the medium and add 500 μl of basic differentiation medium supplemented with 10 ng/ml FGF9. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S01 -->
2. Culture the cells at 37 °C in a 5% CO₂ incubator for 1–2 days. Feeding is usually unnecessary, but if the medium turns yellow, feed with basic differentiation medium supplemented with 10 ng/ml FGF9. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S02 -->
3. Follow Option A to differentiate cells into 2D kidney organoids or Option B to differentiate hPSCs into 3D kidney organoids. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S03 -->

## Differentiation into posterior intermediate mesoderm

### 6~7 d

1. Check cell confluency; approximately 50% is optimal for starting differentiation. Aspirate ReproFF2 and add 500 μl PBS to wash away remnants. **Critical Step**: Confluency at initiation affects viability and efficiency. If confluency is <50%, delay the start of differentiation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S01 -->
2. Aspirate PBS and add 500 μl of differentiation basal medium supplemented with 3–10 μM CHIR and optionally a BMP4 inhibitor (noggin 5–25 ng/ml or dorsomorphin 100–500 nM). **Critical Step**: CHIR concentration and BMP4 inhibitor addition depend on cell line, passage number, and culture conditions. For H9 cells with ReproFF2, 8 μM CHIR is best. For HDF cells, 10 μM CHIR with 5 ng/ml noggin is best. For other lines/media: 1) Adjust plating number to reach 50% confluency at initiation. 2) Find the highest CHIR concentration (3–10 μM) that does not cause detachment/death over 4 days. 3) Test BMP4 inhibitors if CHIR/plating adjustments are insufficient for SIX2+ induction. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S02 -->
3. Culture the cells at 37 °C in a 5% CO₂ incubator for 2 days. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S03 -->
4. Aspirate the medium and feed cells with 500 μl of fresh differentiation medium supplemented with the same concentration of CHIR (with or without BMP4 inhibitor). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S04 -->
5. Culture the cells at 37 °C in a 5% CO₂ incubator for 2 days. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S05 -->
6. Check cell morphology. Loosely formed dense clusters indicate the optimal time to switch treatments. Typically, 96 hours is best, but adjust based on morphology. Aspirate the medium and add 750 μl of differentiation medium with 10 ng/ml activin A. **Critical Step**: This stage is crucial for NPC differentiation. Check morphology carefully. If cells form a homogenous flat monolayer (too loose), feed with differentiation medium containing the same CHIR concentration (with/without BMP4 inhibitor) and wait 0.5–1 day. If cells form dome-like round clusters (too dense), it may be too late; restart differentiation with lower CHIR concentration. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S06 -->
7. Culture the cells at 37 °C in a 5% CO₂ incubator for 2–3 days without feeding. If SIX2+ induction is poor, test treating with activin A for 2 days instead of 3. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S07 -->

## Maintenance of hPSCs

### 7 d

1. Before passaging, check cell conditions and spontaneous differentiation. Healthy undifferentiated hPSCs have round colonies with clear boundaries. Proceed when colonies are ~80% confluent. Merged colonies are common in feeder-free culture. **Critical Step**: Differentiated cells often appear in the center of large colonies or as fibroblast-like cells at the periphery. If difficult to remove, retry the transition from feeder-based to feeder-free culture from the beginning. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S01 -->
2. Visually identify and aspirate differentiated colonies; removing large ones is sufficient as small ones disappear upon passaging. Aspirate ReproFF2 and add 200 μl of Dissociation Solution for human ES/iPS cells (CTK solution) from the well center to cover the surface. Incubate at 37 °C for 2 minutes until colony edges roll up. Aspirate CTK and add 2 ml PBS to wash. **Critical Step**: Do not expose cells to CTK too long, or colonies will be lost during washing. Visually check for detachment after 2 minutes; check every 15 seconds thereafter. Proceed when peripheries start rolling up. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S02 -->
3. Aspirate PBS and add 1 ml ReproFF2. Detach colonies with a cell scraper. Break up colonies with a 1 ml pipette until large aggregates are no longer visible (pipette 3–10 times depending on confluency/line). **Critical Step**: Optimal colony size depends on line, confluency, and passage. In optimized feeder-free culture, optimal diameter is 100–200 μm. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S03 -->
4. Prepare a new plate by letting it sit at room temperature for 30 minutes. Aspirate Geltrex from the new well and add 1–1.7 ml ReproFF2 depending on the passage ratio (total volume 2 ml). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S04 -->
5. Transfer 330 μl–1 ml (1:1–1:3 ratio) of colony fragments into one well of the new plate. Gently shake the plate to distribute colonies evenly. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S05 -->
6. Maintain cells at 37 °C in a 5% CO₂ incubator. Replace medium after 3 and 5 days. Passage cells every 7 days. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S06 -->

## Preparation of hPSCs for differentiation

### 3 d

1. On the day of passaging, check confluency and spontaneous differentiation. Usually, few differentiated cells are present, so removal is unnecessary. If present, aspirate them and grow smaller colonies in subsequent passages. **Critical Step**: If confluency is low, passage at 1:1 ratio until ~80% confluent. Low confluency leads to poor viability and inefficient differentiation. If >5% of colonies show differentiation, further passaging is required before differentiation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S01 -->
2. Aspirate ReproFF2 and add 2 ml PBS. Gently swirl to wash. Aspirate PBS and add 500 μl Accutase. Incubate at 37 °C and 5% CO₂ for 10 minutes. Tap the plate to aid detachment. Incubate for another 5 minutes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S02 -->
3. After a total incubation of 15 minutes, gently detach and dissociate cells with a 1 ml pipette until no aggregates are visible. Prepare 15 ml tubes with 500 μl ReproFF2. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S03 -->
4. Collect dissociated cells into the 15 ml tubes containing 500 μl ReproFF2. Take a 20 μl sample to a Cellometer Counting Chamber for counting. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S04 -->
5. Centrifuge tubes at 300 g at room temperature for 4 minutes. While centrifuging, count cells with a Cellometer. Aspirate medium and resuspend cells at 10,000 cells/μl in ReproFF2. **Critical Step**: One well of a 6-well plate typically yields 2–5 million cells. Fewer than 1 million indicates low initial confluency, leading to poor viability upon differentiation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S05 -->
6. Aspirate supernatant and resuspend cells at 10,000 cells/μl in ReproFF2. Prepare sufficient ReproFF2 with 10 μM Y27632 (1:1000 dilution) for differentiation. Transfer suspension to this medium to achieve 44,000–86,000 cells/ml (12,000–24,000 cells/cm²). Plate 500 μl/well in 24-well plates. **Critical Step**: Plating density is critical for efficiency. Test densities for different lines. H9: ~20,000 cells/cm²; HDF-α iPS: ~14,000 cells/cm². Well size matters; adjust densities if changing well sizes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S06 -->
7. - 13| Culture the cells at 37 °C in a 5% CO _2 incubator for 72 hours. There is no need to change the medium. **CRITICAL STEP** If you want to start the differentiation earlier, you need to plate more cells at step 12 to have nearly 50% confluent cells when you start the differentiation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S07 -->
